loci.name: leakage-safe-temporal-split-vs-random-stratified-split
loci.one_line: Does the golden set need a temporal / conversation-disjoint split, or does random stratified sampling suffice?
opposing_positions: Temporal (time-cutoff) + conversation-thread-disjoint splits are mandatory: random splits leak near-duplicate reply phrasing and same-thread context across train/golden, inflating intent accuracy and grounding scores; selective-prediction IID/OOD gaps and OOD-detection literature show in-domain numbers do not transfer.

Random stratified sampling over the brand subsample suffices for a 150-250 golden set: temporal cuts shrink rare intents below usable counts and confound brand policy-drift with model quality; leakage risk is controllable by dedup + thread-ID grouping without a hard time cutoff.
loci.rationale: Directly changes the re-engineering directive: temporal-disjoint golden construction costs rare-intent coverage but is the only defense against the audit finding inflated trustworthiness. Depth work should quantify duplicate/thread-leakage rate in the Twitter corpus and prescribe the exact split protocol (time cutoff + thread grouping + dedup rule).

loci.name: golden-set-adjudication-and-agreement-gate
loci.one_line: What agreement metric and adjudication rule certify the 150-250 golden set as trustworthy ground truth?
opposing_positions: Krippendorff alpha >= 0.800 overall plus per-label reporting, with routed senior adjudication (not majority vote) and a living guideline changelog, is the certification bar; anything 0.667-0.800 is tentative-only and must block headline claims.

Cohen kappa / raw agreement with majority-vote aggregation suffices at this scale: triple annotation of 250 items with adjudication routing is over-engineered for an intern take-home; report kappa per axis and move on.
loci.rationale: Analyst-a likely centers LLM-judge-vs-human agreement but underweights the prior question: whether the human ground truth itself is certified. The corpus has an unusually strong annotation-quality thread (alpha thresholds, gold-task injection rates, disagreement-as-signal) that yields a concrete, checkable prescription for the harness: metric choice, per-label reporting, gold-task rate, adjudication path. Depth investigation should convert this into the golden-set SOP.

loci.name: ragas-reference-free-metrics-headline-vs-secondary
loci.one_line: Can RAGAS faithfulness / context-precision scores headline the report, or must they stay secondary to human-anchored rubric scores?
opposing_positions: RAGAS as headline: faithfulness, answer relevancy, context precision/recall are published,Runnable metrics with framework adapters; paired with Langfuse tracing they give the cheapest repeatable regression gate for the grounded generator.

RAGAS as secondary only: every RAGAS metric is itself an LLM-judge call inheriting position/verbosity/self-preference bias plus $0.02-0.05 per-trace cost; unvalidated suite scores prove nothing, so the headline must be the custom harness with human agreement and RAGAS demoted to diagnostic signals.
loci.rationale: The build-vs-buy fight is usually argued at framework level; the load-bearing sub-question is metric validity: whether reference-free scores can carry a trustworthiness claim without per-deployment human validation. Corpus holds both the feature matrices and the bias/cost evidence to settle placement precisely (which RAGAS metrics survive as gated diagnostics vs headline). This determines harness architecture and eval budget.

loci.name: embedded-store-sufficiency-vs-managed-storage-for-3m-tweets
loci.one_line: Do FAISS/Chroma/LanceDB + DuckDB/SQLite carry the whole submission, or is Postgres+pgvector / managed search required?
opposing_positions: Embedded suffices and reproduces fastest: subsample eval runs in-process on thousands of threads; Polars+DuckDB handle multi-million-row ETL without distributed systems; vendor-neutral benchmarks show embedded options competitive at this scale with swappable interfaces for scale-up.

Managed/heavy required: unifying BM25+dense behind one retriever interface (ES) or keeping vectors in the production database (pgvector) is the only path where hybrid retrieval, persistence, and multi-tenant serving behave like production; embedded is a demo shortcut the audit should flag.
loci.rationale: Underweighted operational hinge: the storage choice dictates reproducibility (15-minute setup), hybrid-retrieval feasibility, and what the decision log can honestly claim about production readiness. Evidence is scale-scoped rather than contradictory, so depth work should pin the scale boundary quantitatively (rows/latency/ops cost) instead of relitigating preferences.

loci.name: pii-redaction-and-prompt-injection-guardrail-placement-and-eval
loci.one_line: Where do PII redaction and prompt-injection guardrails sit in the pipeline, and how are they evaluated rather than asserted?
opposing_positions: Pre-retrieval redaction + refusal/escalation path as a hard gate: strip PII before retrieval/generation, treat injection attempts as auto-escalate, and eval with promptfoo red-team plugins (pii, prompt-injection, jailbreak) plus false-refusal rate on benign edge cases.

Post-generation filter suffices: log-and-scrub outputs, rely on the LLM provider safety layer, and keep guardrail eval to a handful of spot checks; dedicated red-team harness is out of scope for the take-home.
loci.rationale: Security/PII is the trustworthiness dimension most likely to be asserted-but-unmeasured in the untrusted workspace, and the corpus gives both the mechanism (redaction placement, refusal paths) and the measurement tool (promptfoo red-team, false-refusal/over-blocking eval). Synthesis should produce the guardrail test plan and its two-sided metric (leak rate down, false-refusal rate bounded), which feeds the auto-handle/escalate decider directly.
